location_qualifier: place of the main effort at the Rhine; the headquarters place is not named
current_activity: Army Group Oberrhein (Himmler) opens its Nordwind supporting attack at Gambsheim on 5 January to take Strasbourg
notes: Event date: CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 28 p. 513: "On 5 January, as Patch began deploying the 103d Division east of the Vosges, Himmler's Army Group Oberrhein began its NORDWIND"; "If Hitler could not take Antwerp in the north, then Himmler was determined to present him with Strasbourg in the south". Event definition: the start of the attack on 5 January. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Gambsheim with a precision of 10 km, the place where the main effort crossed the Rhine; the army group headquarters place is not named. Location approximate: the attack place, not the headquarters. Location support: CMH names the main effort of the XIV SS Corps at Gambsheim on p. 513. Commander: SS-Reichsführer Heinrich Himmler. Opponents: US Seventh Army (VI Corps).

location_qualifier: representative point for the Upper Rhine sector; the headquarters place is not named
source_locator: R425: p. 537; R649: Einsatz, Gliederung, December 1944 and January 1945
current_activity: Army Group Oberrhein, re-formed under Hausser after Himmler leaves, orders Rasp to prepare renewed attacks at Erstein
notes: Event date: CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 29 p. 537: "on 22 January Army Group Oberrhein ordered Rasp to be prepared to renew his attacks in the northern corner of the pocket"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, Heeresgruppe Oberrhein: "Als Ersatz wurde am 22. Januar 1945 das Heeresgruppenkommando Oberrhein aufgestellt"; "Paul Hausser". Event definition: CMH gives the order of 22 January; the Lexikon gives 22 January for the re-formation of the headquarters, and 23 January as the date Hausser followed Himmler. Event support: two source families (CMH and the Lexikon, Tessin) agree on 22 January. Location: Colmar with a precision of 50 km, a representative point for the Upper Rhine sector; neither source names the headquarters place. Location approximate: a representative point for the sector. Location support: both sources name the Upper Rhine and the Colmar pocket only. Commander: SS-Oberstgruppenführer Paul Hausser (Lexikon, from 23 January). Opponents: French First Army. Context: Himmler moved east with his staff from 21 January and formed Army Group Vistula on 24 January (Lexikon). CMH ch. 29 p. 548 places Hausser at the head of Army Group G on 29 January, so the Lexikon note that he commanded Army Group Oberrhein from 23 January is not tested here.

Januar 1945 wurde das Heeresgruppenkommando Oberrhein wieder aufgelöst". Event definition: the dissolution on 29 January in both families.
